To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of 2,3-butanediol and glycerol on the structure and function of enzymes are similar to those of ionic solvents, but they are opposite when the cryoprotective concentration is exceeded, and they are similar to the effects of macromolecular crowding agents when the cryosolvent is present at low concentrations.

the cryosolvents have an impact on the structures and activities of enzymes and other biopolymers, and that this impact is strongly modulated by the ionic and macramolecular solutes present in the system, in a way that is hard to predict and to understand.

cryosolvents (dimethylsulfoxide, glycerol and dimethylformamide) and ions (Na ^{+}, K ^{+}, Mg ^{2+}, Ca ^{2+} ) may interact with macromolecular solute and with each other to produce a wide range of effects on the structures and the functions of enzymes, and that these effects may be additive or opposite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of water and cryosolvents on protein structures and their biological functions.
the study of the structure and function of macromolecular systems and their response to cryosolvents.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cryosolvents are not only cryoprotective agents, but also cryoinhibitory agents, depending on their concentrations.
cryosolvents do not affect the structure of proteins and enzymes, and therefore they are not able to induce cryoinjury.
cryosolvents have a strong impact on the behavior of proteins and other macromolecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cryosolvents can be used to modify the structures and functions in biological systems.
the cryosolvent effects are additive or opposite to those of ionic solvents depending on the respective concentration.
the interactive effects of cryosolute, ionic and molecular solutes on the structure and function of proteins and enzymes are not always additive, but may be synergic or antagonistic.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of cryosolvent and cryoprotectants may have to be reconsidered in the light of the interactive effects of the cryosolvent, the ionic solutes and the biopolymers on protein and cell structures.
the cryosolvents can mimic ionic effects, and that they may also be used as cryoprotectants.
the cryoprotective effects of ionic compounds and macromolecules are not additive, but they can be synergistic or even antagonistic depending on the nature of the compounds.
